g.text: How Commands, Queries, Events & Projections flow from browser to read model and back

g.title: Your frontend application — sends commands and queries, receives real-time events
Decode request → Command/Query, inject ContextEnricher (correlationID, userID, requestID, IP, UA), encode response
Subscribe to Event Bus, push filtered events to client in real-time
Injects HTTP request context into events: correlationID, causationID, userID, requestID, IP, UserAgent — via event.WithCorrelationID, WithUserID, etc.
Root interface: Apply(evt), RecordEvent(ctx, evt), UncommittedChanges(), MarkChangesAsCommitted()
Save: Store.Save → Outbox/Bus.Publish → Snapshot Load: SnapshotStore.Load → Store.LoadFromVersion → Replay
event.Store: Save (optimistic concurrency), Load, LoadFromVersion, Delete, io.Closer
event.Outbox: Append (same TX as Store.Save), PollPending, Ack — guarantees at-least-once publishing
event.SnapshotStore: Save, Load (latest), LoadAtVersion, io.Closer — accelerated aggregate replay
event.Bus: Publish, Subscribe(type), SubscribeAll, io.Closer — delivers domain events to projections and SSE/WS
Projection: Name, Handle(ctx, evt), EventTypes() — InMemoryRunner routes events and saves checkpoints
event.CheckpointStore: Load(projectionName), Save(projectionName, eventID) — tracks projection offset
Materialized view updated by projections. Queried by Query Handlers.
AsyncAPI 3.0 YAML/JSON, EventCatalog MDX, D2 diagrams — auto-generated from Go types via SchemaFromType[T]
Routes commands to handlers. Middleware applied at Register time.
Loads aggregate, applies business logic, records events, saves via repository
Routes queries to handlers. Returns typed results via DispatchTyped[T].
Reads from materialized read model built by projections

text.tspan: 3 Handler loads aggregate, applies business logic, records events
4 Repository persists to Event Store (optimistic concurrency)
7 Bus delivers events to Projections & SSE/WS
13 Real-time push to client via SSE/WebSocket
Module labels [brackets] show which go module owns each component:
